$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the money-path file list (#1030).
This list previously existed in three places that disagreed. .github/labeler.yml
-- which applies the `money-path` label, and therefore decides whether money.md
and its characterization-test bar get loaded -- was MISSING the delegation rail,
the rail seam, and the SDK signer. Nobody noticed, because nothing compared them.
A money-path list that is wrong in one copy is worse than none: it reads as
coverage.
TWO LISTS, because the two consumers ask different questions:
globs -- RUNTIME money-path code. Code that moves money or grants authority,
i.e. behaviour the deployed money-flow QA harness actually exercises. This is
what scripts/ci/qa-freshness.mjs checks: 'did the green QA run cover this?'
controlGlobs -- the money-path SAFEGUARD's own control surface. A PR that
weakens the gate deserves the money-path playbook and a human reading it, but
re-running the money-flow harness proves nothing about a CI config change --
the harness does not test the gate. So these are LABELLED money-path without
forcing a QA re-run, which would be friction with no evidence attached.
labeler.yml uses the UNION. qa-freshness.mjs uses `globs` only.
scripts/ci/money-path.test.mjs asserts this file, labeler.yml and the SKILL.md
Merge Gate agree. Editing one without the others fails CI.
Adding a glob is cheap and safe. Leaving one out is the failure mode.
2026-07-27 (#1045): added the money-moving surfaces the adversarial review
found missing (sweep, relayer, safe-exec, approvals, hybrid-accounts,
mainnet-gate) -- 'leaving one out is the failure mode', and these were out.
release-bump.mjs and publish.yml moved to controlGlobs: the harness cannot
exercise them, so keeping them in `globs` made 'a green run covered this'
hollow -- they still get the label and the human reading, without a QA
re-run that proves nothing about them.
2026-08-24 (#1987): domain/payment-coverage.ts and
rails/allowance-nonce-coordinator.ts REMOVED -- both files are DELETED by
the AllowanceModule rail retirement (epic #1440 slice 4). This is not a
safeguard being weakened: a glob naming a file that does not exist protects
nothing, and the `no phantom globs` test in money-path.test.mjs fails CI on
it. rails/allowance-module.ts STAYS -- the file survives as reads-only
(getProvider/getRelayerWallet/getTokenBalance are shared infra; the four
contract reads back GET /machine-payments/allowances and the legacy
wallet-approval authority check). Removing a glob for code that still
exists would be the failure mode this file's header warns about.
2026-08-19 (#1607): infra/relayer.ts widened to infra/relayer*.ts (spend guard,
balance monitor) and infra/outbound-*.ts added -- epic #1554 shipped the durable
outbound queue + bump worker, which broadcast and replace real transactions.
2026-08-23 (#1892): routes/agent-rekey.ts and modules/agents/rekey-*.ts added.
#1698 shipped the re-key surface -- it revokes and re-issues an agent's on-chain
spend authority, the identical job routes/agent-delegations.ts was already listed
for -- and NOTHING learned about it: not this file, not labeler.yml, not the
SKILL.md Merge Gate. PR #1891 changed routes/agent-rekey.ts and carried
`area:backend, area:docs` and NO money-path label; the classification was right
only because a human had labelled the ISSUE. Note infra/repositories/** already
covered the re-key REPOSITORY, so a PR touching the storage layer was labelled
while one touching only the route was not -- the most misleading kind of
half-coverage, because the list read as though it knew about re-key.
2026-08-23 (#1892, from review): infra/delegate-*.ts added. The delegate
balance monitor (#714, epic #713) is the DETECT mitigation for the x402
in-flight window -- the interval where Safe-funded USDC sits on a hot
delegate EOA outside every policy layer -- and it alerts on `lingering`,
i.e. sweepable money nobody swept. Its sibling infra/relayer-balance-monitor.ts
is EQUALLY read-only and was already matched by infra/relayer*.ts; the two
even share the DELEGATE_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL channel. Listing one and not the
other was an accident of glob prefix, not a judgement. Globbed rather than
named so the next delegate-* infra file is covered the day it is written,
same reasoning as #1607's relayer.ts -> relayer*.ts widening.
2026-08-23 (#1897): modules/machine-payments/** REMOVED -- retired
deliberately, not lost. It matched nothing, and it never had: the directory
does not appear anywhere in git history, under any status. #1158 added it
PRE-EMPTIVELY for the #997 split ('machine-payments (pre-emptive)', commit
808394bf), and that split landed as modules/mpp/ instead, so the anticipated
destination was never created. This is therefore a deletion, not a re-point:
there is no moved code to follow. Every machine-payment file that exists
today was already covered by a DIFFERENT entry -- routes/machine-payments.ts
and domain/machine-payment-lifecycle.ts by name, infra/repositories/
machine-payments.ts by infra/repositories/**, the five machine_payment_*
migrations by db/migrations/**, and the module itself by modules/mpp/**.
Proven, not asserted: classifying every tracked file through
qa-freshness.mjs's own matchesGlob() before and after the removal returns
the IDENTICAL set. The perimeter did not shrink.
A phantom entry is not free, which is why it came out: this list is read by
humans and agents deciding whether their own diff is money-path, and an entry
naming a module layout that never existed makes the perimeter look like it
covers ground it does not. money-path.test.mjs now asserts every glob matches
at least one tracked file, so a fifth phantom cannot accumulate silently.
Adding a glob AHEAD of the code it anticipates is still allowed -- see
PRE_EMPTIVE_GLOBS in that test, which is the sanctioned place to say so.
2026-08-23 (#1904, from review): scripts/ci/money-path-restatement-scan.mjs
added to controlGlobs. It is a REPORTING tool that never gates -- but it
supplies the scoring functions behind an assertion inside money-path.test.mjs,
which is itself a control glob. Without this entry the invariant could be
neutered by editing the scan file alone, with no money-path label and nobody
reading money.md -- the control surface would be guarded at the front door
and open at the side. Listed for the same reason #1892 listed
infra/delegate-*.ts: which file the enforcement happens to live in is an
accident, and the perimeter should not depend on it.

2026-08-25 (#1905/#1896/#1903): packages/signer/** and packages/core/src/machine-payment-lifecycle.ts joined `globs` — the edge-signer package that actually holds the delegate key (the SDK-side signer was already listed on 'signing schemes are spend authority', the package was not — #1896), and the machine-payment domain logic relocated verbatim to @haven_ai/core by #987 (the backend listing guarded a 12-line re-export shim, not the code — #1905). packages/frontend/src/lib/signer.ts and packages/frontend/src/hooks/useAgentRekey.ts joined `controlGlobs`: the client that picks which signer signs a spend-authority action is invisible to this list today (#1903), but the money-flow harness exercises the deployed backend, not the client — so it gets the label and a human, without a QA re-run that proves nothing. A frontend file that MOVES money has not been found; these are decision surfaces, and if one appears it belongs in `globs`.

2026-08-29 (#2200): the docs coupling gate's control surface added to controlGlobs -- scripts/docs/coupling-gate.mjs, scripts/docs/validate-frontmatter.mjs and .github/workflows/docs-coupling.yml. That gate is the ENFORCEMENT POINT for the CASP shard requirement -- what decides whether a money-path PR may merge without writing its perimeter analysis -- which is the job qa-freshness.mjs does for the QA harness, and that was already listed. None of the three was on either list, so PR #2201 changed that gate carrying area:docs and NO money-path label and got no mandatory human read, while fixing a silent bypass in it (an edit to an already-merged shard satisfied the blocking gate: exit 1 -> exit 0). Same shape as #1892. Each entry decided on its own evidence: coupling-gate.mjs IS the gate; validate-frontmatter.mjs because the gate imports its globToRegExp/parseFrontMatter and mutating that matcher flips the blocking gate exit 1 -> exit 0 from OUTSIDE the gate (its own test suite reddens, but docs:coupling is also run standalone with no sibling suite -- release-bump.mjs's release preflight, ai-agent-workflow.md's Green-Gate Evidence step, pr-workflow-checklist.md -- and there the regression is genuinely silent); docs-coupling.yml because its `contract` job is what makes the script a REQUIRED check, so dropping --strict or narrowing the job's `if:` weakens CASP enforcement without touching any listed file, exactly as dev-gate.yml/qa-dev.yml/publish.yml are listed for wiring their scripts into real gates. CONSIDERED AND EXCLUDED, recorded so nobody re-derives it: chain-integrity.mjs -- neither the gate nor the parser imports it (checked), it runs in a different required job, and it guards last-verified history rather than the shard requirement; coupling-gate.test.mjs -- the gate runs for real on every PR so a broken test disables nothing silently, and any edit reintroducing a #2192-shaped bug must touch coupling-gate.mjs itself, which is now listed. (money-path.test.mjs IS listed because it is the drift guard with no separate runtime -- a different case.) Sweeping scripts/docs/ in wholesale was rejected: over-labelling costs a human read on every docs-tooling PR. Label cost measured first -- 90-day commit counts: coupling-gate.mjs 2, validate-frontmatter.mjs 3, docs-coupling.yml 1, against the already-listed qa-freshness.mjs at 2. controlGlobs and not globs: re-running the money-flow harness proves nothing about a docs gate.
2026-08-31 (#2264, epic #1440): routes/agent-connection-setups.ts added to globs.
It is where an owner's approval BECOMES an agent's on-chain spend authority:
POST /:setupId/budget-approval verifies the signed delegation against the setup
(verifyDelegationSetupAuthority reads listActiveDelegations and matches token,
budget amount and period) and only then flips the setup — and the agent — to
active; the same file emits the allowance_granted funnel event and enforces
one-budget-per-agent for the delegation rail. That is the identical job
routes/agent-delegations.ts and routes/agent-rekey.ts are BOTH already listed
for, and this is the third member of that family — the one the Safe retirement
moved INTO it, since connect is now the only onboarding path (#1984). A PR
touching only this route got no money-path label, no money.md routing and no
qa-freshness requirement. Same shape as #1892 (agent-rekey) and #2200 (the docs
gate), and the same answer. globs and not controlGlobs: this is RUNTIME code on
the live rail that the deployed money-flow QA harness exercises when an agent is
connected and granted a budget, not a CI control surface.
2026-09-02 (#2300): packages/mcp-server/src/** added to globs -- the hosted MCP
tool surface. tools.ts is the ordering-and-authorization decision surface for a
funding relay: #2282 (PR #2296) was haven_settle_mcp_tool relaying the funding
userop BEFORE checking the merchant-call context existed, stranding the caller
with a funded_but_unsettled intent (reproduced on dev with real Base Sepolia
transactions); #2312 (PR #2355) measured that the MCP SDK strips undeclared
keys before the handler, so a caller's tx_hash was silently dropped on a
settlement path; #2348 (PR #2368) measured that a stripped idempotencyKey on
haven_send meant a RETRY IS A SECOND SPEND, and on haven_pay_mcp_tool REPLACED
the replay scope with a 300 s quote-hash bucket; #2051 (PR 04273d2c) was a
merchant-steerable cap bypass in the same file -- 900 USDC authorized against a
stated 1 USDC cap. Four money defects in one file, none of whose PRs carried
the money-path label by the file half: PR #2296 changed tools.ts and carried
`area:mcp, area:docs`. The #1896 shape again -- a file whose omission gives the
right answer for the wrong reason -- and the same answer.
globs and not controlGlobs, decided on the file's own test: the deployed
money-flow QA harness EXERCISES this code. The hosted MCP deploys from `dev`
on Railway (docs/operations/dev-environment.md) and qa-dev.yml drives it
through QA_HOSTED_MCP_URL with the real @haven_ai/signer in-process --
x402-hosted-mcp-signer, x402-erc7710-hosted and x402-catalog-guided-purchase
all call haven_pay_mcp_tool / haven_settle_mcp_tool on the deployed server.
That is the argument the frontend decision surfaces (#1903) could NOT make,
which is why they are control globs: the harness exercises the deployed
backend, not the client. Here it exercises the deployed hosted server, so 'did
the green run cover this?' is a real question with a real answer.
Scoped to src/** rather than the whole package, and the delta was measured
before choosing: across 1156 first-parent commits on dev in the 90 days to
2026-09-02, 55 touched packages/mcp-server, 53 of them under src/, and only 2
touched exclusively README.md / Dockerfile / package.json / tsconfig / tsup /
vitest config. Those six are build and prose plumbing the harness cannot
distinguish a change to, and the whole-package glob would also have forced
casp-risk-guardrails.md's `covers:` -- which already carries
packages/mcp-server/src/** and nothing wider -- to widen to a Dockerfile to
keep the #1899 pin green. CONSIDERED AND EXCLUDED, recorded so nobody
re-derives it. Label cost, same measurement: 28 of those 55 commits carried
no money-path label through any other listed file and now would; 28 would
newly require a covering QA run before promotion. Against the already-listed
packages/signer/** at 79 commits in the same window, the churn is comparable.
One consequence the tier carries, and it is closed in the same change:
scripts/release-bump.mjs writes HOSTED_SERVER_VERSION into
packages/mcp-server/src/server.ts on every cut, always after the last green
run -- the exact shape #2164 found for SIGNER_VERSION, where the gate refused
every release by construction and qa-override became the route. The
RELEASE_BUMP_VERSION_CONSTANTS allowlist in scripts/ci/qa-freshness.mjs now
names HOSTED_SERVER_VERSION too (its own header says to re-derive it by
intersecting release-bump's SOURCE_VERSION_CONSTANTS with these globs, and
this entry is what changed the intersection). CONNECTOR_VERSION and
CLI_VERSION stay out: connect/ and cli/ are on no glob.
Corrects the issue's own premise: qa-freshness does NOT key on the PR label.
It diffs the promotion head against the green run's SHA and matches the
changed files against `globs` (evaluate()'s changedMoneyPathFiles). So the
label a human put on issue #2282 never reached the gate -- only a file entry
can -- which makes the file half the ONLY half that gates promotion.
